documents.title: Installation
documents.text: Set up the gem once. Then call any component directly from ERB.

documents.title: Before you start
documents.text: Use Rails 8 or later with Propshaft, importmap, Stimulus and tailwindcss-rails 4.4 or later. Tailwind CSS v4 is required: it compiles the component styles and the utilities in your views. A Rails app created with Tailwind includes this setup.

documents.title: 1. Add the gem
documents.text: Add this to your Gemfile , then run bundle install . The engine makes all lc_* helpers available to views. There are no per-component Ruby or JavaScript imports. Commit Gemfile.lock to pin the version your app uses.

documents.title: 2. Add the stylesheet
documents.text: For a new app, save the starter stylesheet as app/assets/tailwind/application.css . The engine import includes the default light and dark theme. For an existing app, add the starter's layer order and typography plugin if needed. Keep your Tailwind imports and add the engine import: Run bin/rails tailwindcss:build . The build generates that import path from the installed gem. Components work with the defaults immediately. To customize colors or fonts, add overrides after the import using the theming guide .

documents.title: 3. Load the assets
documents.text: Your layout needs the compiled Tailwind stylesheet and importmap tags. Keep your existing tags if they already load these assets. The engine adds its Stimulus pins to the importmap. Load controllers with lazyLoadControllersFrom("controllers", application) in controllers/index.js , so each page downloads only the controllers it uses. To ship less CSS, import core.css and the components you use instead of the whole library; the README lists the entries.

documents.title: 4. Use a component
documents.text: Helpers render native HTML. Use class: for additional utilities, data: and aria: for attributes, and blocks for custom content. Browse the button examples to see variants, sizes, links and Rails forms.

documents.title: Theming
documents.detail: The default light and dark themes use neutral surfaces and accents, with color available for statuses and avatars.
documents.text: The default light and dark themes use neutral surfaces and accents, with color available for statuses and avatars. The theme has eleven color roles. After installation , no token file is required.

documents.title: Change your colors
documents.text: Add overrides after the engine import in app/assets/tailwind/application.css . This example changes actions, links, selected states and keyboard focus to green. Soft backgrounds follow automatically. The default text color on primary buttons is white in light mode and dark in dark mode; set --primary-foreground if your color needs a different contrast. Use --background for the page, --muted for cards, --foreground for text and --muted-foreground for hints. Matching utilities include bg-muted , text-muted-foreground and border-border .

documents.title: Choose colors by purpose
documents.text: You only need to override the roles you want to change. Status colors control both text and soft feedback backgrounds. Theme colors CSS property Value Used for --background Page background --foreground Main text and headings --card Cards and grouped content --card-foreground Text on cards --popover Menus, popovers and dialogs --popover-foreground Text on menus, popovers and dialogs --primary Primary actions, links, selected states and keyboard focus --primary-foreground Text and icons on a solid primary background --secondary Secondary buttons --secondary-foreground Text on secondary buttons --muted Subtle backgrounds: badges, code, skeletons, table headers --muted-foreground Secondary text, hints and placeholders --accent Hovered rows, menu items and inline code --accent-foreground Text on accent backgrounds --destructive Errors and destructive actions --success Successful actions and positive feedback --warning Warnings and items needing attention --border Dividers and outlines --input Input and toggle fills --ring Keyboard focus ring; unset, it follows --primary

documents.title: Switch themes
documents.text: Set data-theme="dark" on <html> for dark mode and Tailwind's dark: variant. Remove it for light mode. Your app controls the switch and saved preference.

documents.title: Fonts, corners and shadows
documents.text: Load your font, then set the body and heading families. The defaults use system fonts. Set radius variables on body for controls and cards. rounded-full buttons keep their pill shape. --lc-shadow controls the shared surface shadow. For one component, use class: . See Foundations for typography, Japanese text and spacing. Browse the color roles, typography, spacing and appearance settings for defaults, current theme values and page-scoped override names.

documents.title: Foundations
documents.detail: Typography, spacing and reading rhythm shared by every app.
documents.text: Typography, spacing and reading rhythm shared by every app. Text styles pair size, line height, weight and tracking. Heading level describes the document structure; size: describes its appearance. Parents set space between children with stacks, inline groups and sections. Use <code> for inline references with a monospace font and subtle background. Page title 30 / 36 Section title 20 / 24 Card title 18 / 24 Body 16 / 24 Small 14 / 20 Caption 12 / 16 Font size / line height in pixels at the default browser size. Values use rem units. tight 4px related 8px heading 12px content 16px inset 20px section 32px A section leaves 12px below its heading and 16px between its content blocks. Stack sections with gap: :section. lc_prose styles rendered HTML with a 65ch reading measure, 1.75 line height and proportional block spacing. Enable @plugin "@tailwindcss/typography"; in the host Tailwind input. The standalone Rails CLI includes the plugin. Mark embedded controls or cards not-prose to keep their component styles.

documents.title: Theme colors
documents.text: These eleven colors are the everyday theme settings. Defaults work without overrides. Names describe their purpose: bg-muted for a card, text-muted-foreground for a hint, border-border for a divider. Values below follow the selected palette and light or dark mode. Change --primary to update actions, links, selection and focus together. Soft backgrounds for primary and status colors are generated automatically. See the theming guide for examples. Theme colors CSS property Value Used for --background Page background --foreground Main text and headings --card Cards and grouped content --card-foreground Text on cards --popover Menus, popovers and dialogs --popover-foreground Text on menus, popovers and dialogs --primary Primary actions, links, selected states and keyboard focus --primary-foreground Text and icons on a solid primary background --secondary Secondary buttons --secondary-foreground Text on secondary buttons --muted Subtle backgrounds: badges, code, skeletons, table headers --muted-foreground Secondary text, hints and placeholders --accent Hovered rows, menu items and inline code --accent-foreground Text on accent backgrounds --destructive Errors and destructive actions --success Successful actions and positive feedback --warning Warnings and items needing attention --border Dividers and outlines --input Input and toggle fills --ring Keyboard focus ring; unset, it follows --primary

documents.title: Feedback follows the action
documents.text: Buttons respond to hover and press automatically. Copy buttons transition their label and icon after the clipboard write succeeds. The same button keeps focus and reserves room for every label, so nearby content stays still. Try the controls below with a mouse, keyboard, or touch. Override these CSS variables after the engine import, or on a container to tune one area. Feedback duration controls the visual transition. The copy button's reset_after: controls how long confirmation remains visible. --lc-motion-quick 140ms · icon controls --lc-motion-control 180ms · buttons --lc-motion-feedback 160ms · label and icon swaps --lc-press-scale 0.96 · pressed icon controls --lc-ease-out Shared control easing When the operating system requests reduced motion, controls skip lift and press scaling, and copy feedback changes immediately. Labels, icons, focus, and success announcements still work. Other component animations use the theme's existing reduced-motion handling. Your application owns saving and submitting. Show loading while work is pending, success after it finishes, and an error when it fails. Compose lc_button with lc_spinner and aria-busy for loading feedback. Keep timings in CSS and expose interaction state through data or ARIA attributes in your own controllers. Blocks reuse the library's controls and supply their application behavior.

documents.title: Copy button
documents.detail: Copy text or a live field value with animated confirmation and accessible feedback.
documents.text: Copy text or a live field value with animated confirmation and accessible feedback. Pass exactly one of value: for supplied text or source: for an element ID. Inputs and textareas copy their current value; other elements copy their text content, including whitespace. Clipboard access requires HTTPS or localhost and browser permission. The button shows confirmation only after copying succeeds. Failure shows a retry state and announces how to copy manually. reset_after: sets the confirmation time in milliseconds (2000 by default). Customize copied_label: and error_label: , or use the included English, Japanese, and Spanish translations. Use aria: { label: "Copy invite link" } for a contextual accessible name, including on icon-only buttons. Listen on an ancestor for bubbling lc-copy:copied ( event.detail.text ) and lc-copy:error ( event.detail.error ) events. The button keeps focus and reserves room for every label. Reduced motion changes feedback immediately. See Motion to tune the transition.
